why_this_matters: Day 66 sits in Phase 4 (Pandas + Data Cleaning + EDA), whose goal is: Load, clean, reshape and explore any tabular dataset with confidence. Today's core material - Vertical vs horizontal concatenation, Index handling and ignore_index, Mismatched columns - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.code:
import pandas as pd

# Example datasets for Pakistani context
# Dataset 1 - Pakistani Names and Ages
data1 = {'Name': ['Ahmed', 'Fatima', 'Ali'], 'Age': [28, 32, 24]}
# Dataset 2 - More Pakistani Names and Ages
data2 = {'Name': ['Sara', 'Usman', 'Aisha'], 'Age': [29, 35, 27]}
# Dataset 3 - Cities and Provinces in Pakistan
data3 = {'City': ['Karachi', 'Lahore', 'Islamabad'], 'Province': ['Sindh', 'Punjab', 'Islamabad']}

df1 = pd.DataFrame(data1)
df2 = pd.DataFrame(data2)
df3 = pd.DataFrame(data3)

# Concatenating Rows
concatenated_rows = pd.concat([df1, df2])

# Concatenating Columns
# Note: For a meaningful column-wise concatenation, dataframes should have the same number of rows.
concatenated_columns = pd.concat([df1, df3], axis=1)
print(concatenated_rows)
print(";;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;")
concatenated_columns

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Vertical vs horizontal concatenation on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
